questions.q: The Maths paper was __________ for Devan, who finished it in twenty minutes.
questions.tip: 'A piece of cake' means something very easy to do, needing hardly any effort.

questions.q: My grandfather visits from Perth __________ — perhaps twice in ten years.
questions.tip: 'Once in a blue moon' means very rarely — a blue moon is an extra full moon, which hardly ever happens.

questions.q: Priya felt __________ before going on stage, but she performed beautifully.
options: a chip off the old block
questions.tip: 'Butterflies in her stomach' describes the fluttery, nervous feeling you get just before something important.

questions.q: After breaking the window, Ravi had to __________ and tell his father.
questions.tip: 'Face the music' means to own up and accept the punishment or consequences of what you have done.

questions.q: Nobody knew anyone at the camp, so the leader played a game to __________.
questions.tip: 'Break the ice' means to say or do something that makes strangers feel relaxed with one another.

questions.q: My sister is a real __________; she finishes three novels a week.
questions.tip: A 'bookworm' is someone who loves reading and gets through a great many books.

questions.q: Wei Jie was __________ when he heard he had been selected for the team.
questions.tip: 'Over the moon' means extremely happy and delighted about something.

questions.q: Mother stayed home because she was feeling __________.
questions.tip: 'Under the weather' means feeling slightly unwell or poorly.

questions.q: Don't worry — I was only __________ when I said the test was cancelled.
options: letting the cat out of the bag
hitting the nail on the head
questions.tip: 'Pulling your leg' means teasing you by saying something untrue as a joke.

questions.q: Siti __________ when she accidentally mentioned the surprise party.
options: let the cat out of the bag
questions.tip: 'Let the cat out of the bag' means to give away a secret, usually by accident.

questions.q: You have __________ — that is exactly what went wrong.
options: hit the nail on the head
questions.tip: 'Hit the nail on the head' means to say exactly the right thing, like a hammer striking a nail perfectly.

questions.q: Please __________ your little brother while I go to the shop.
questions.tip: 'Keep an eye on' means to watch someone or something carefully so nothing goes wrong.

questions.q: We are all __________ — nobody in the class understood the homework either.
questions.tip: 'In the same boat' means in the same difficult situation as everybody else.

questions.q: Amir is __________ — he plays the violin just like his mother.
options: a chip off the old block
questions.tip: 'A chip off the old block' means a child very like a parent, as a chip matches its wood block.

questions.q: Stop being such __________ and come and join the game.
options: a chip off the old block
questions.tip: 'A wet blanket' is someone who spoils other people's fun, just as a wet blanket smothers a fire.

questions.q: Mrs Devi has __________; she gives away half her lunch every day.
questions.tip: 'A heart of gold' means being very kind and generous to other people.

questions.q: He got __________ the night before the audition and withdrew.
questions.tip: 'Cold feet' means suddenly feeling too nervous to do something you had planned to do.

questions.q: The two brothers finally decided to __________ after arguing for a year.
questions.tip: 'Bury the hatchet' means to make peace and stop quarrelling — a hatchet is a small axe, put away for good.

questions.q: Nadia __________ by taking on three committees at once.
options: bit off more than she could chew
questions.tip: 'Bit off more than she could chew' means took on far more work than she could manage.

questions.q: He __________ for a week before the examinations, sleeping only four hours a night.
options: took it with a pinch of salt
questions.tip: 'Burnt the midnight oil' means worked or studied very late into the night, from the days of oil lamps.

questions.q: There is no point __________ — the vase is broken and cannot be mended.
questions.tip: 'Crying over spilt milk' means being upset about something that has happened and cannot be undone.

questions.q: Ali was __________ when he saw his cousin's new bicycle.
questions.tip: 'Green with envy' means feeling very jealous of what somebody else has.

questions.q: The teacher __________ to the whispering at the back, just this once.
options: hit the nail on the head
questions.tip: 'Turned a blind eye' means chose to ignore something wrong instead of doing anything about it.

questions.q: Missing the bus was bad; losing my wallet was __________.
questions.tip: 'The last straw' is the final small trouble that makes a difficult situation impossible to bear.

questions.q: Failing that test turned out to be __________ — it made me change how I revise.
questions.tip: 'A blessing in disguise' is something that seems bad at first but turns out to be good.

questions.q: Shouting at him will only __________.
options: hit the nail on the head
questions.tip: 'Add fuel to the fire' means to do something that makes a bad situation even worse.

questions.q: Stop __________ and tell me what actually happened.
questions.tip: 'Beating around the bush' means avoiding the main point instead of saying it plainly.

questions.q: She had to __________ and apologise, even though it was difficult.
questions.tip: 'Bite the bullet' means to make yourself do something difficult or unpleasant that you cannot avoid.

questions.q: We caught the train __________ — it left thirty seconds later.
options: by the skin of our ears
questions.tip: 'In the nick of time' means just in time, with only moments to spare.

questions.q: That camera must have __________; it looks professional.
options: cost an arm and a leg
questions.tip: 'Cost an arm and a leg' means to be very expensive indeed.

questions.q: Don't __________ — there may be a good reason why he was late.
questions.tip: 'Jump to conclusions' means to decide what has happened before you know all the facts.

questions.q: It took her a month to __________ in her new school.
questions.tip: 'Learn the ropes' means learn how things are done in a new place, as new sailors learnt a ship's ropes.

questions.q: My aunt called __________ after ten years of silence.
questions.tip: 'Out of the blue' means happening suddenly, with no warning at all.

questions.q: Take what he says __________; he often exaggerates.
questions.tip: 'With a pinch of salt' means not believing something completely, because it may be exaggerated.

questions.q: The broken window is only __________ — the whole building needs repairs.
questions.tip: 'The tip of the iceberg' means the small visible part of a much bigger problem, since most ice hides underwater.

questions.q: Our teacher encourages us to __________ rather than copy the example.
questions.tip: 'Think outside the box' means to think in a fresh, creative way instead of the usual way.

questions.q: They have stayed friends __________ for thirty years.
questions.tip: 'Through thick and thin' means staying loyal through good times and hard times alike.

questions.q: He never studies and then complains about his results — well, __________.
options: every cloud has a silver lining
two heads are better than one
questions.tip: 'You reap what you sow' means you get the results your own actions earned, like a farmer harvesting what was planted.

questions.q: She __________ by staying behind to help clear up after everyone had left.
questions.tip: 'Went the extra mile' means did more than was needed or expected in order to help.

questions.q: He is always __________ about his results, which annoys the whole class.
questions.tip: 'Blowing his own trumpet' means boasting loudly about how good he is.

questions.q: Our car __________ on the expressway and we had to be towed.
questions.tip: 'Broke down' means stopped working — machines like cars break down when something fails.

questions.q: She was __________ by her grandparents after her parents moved overseas.
questions.tip: 'Brought up' means raised and looked after a child until they grew up.

questions.q: The match was __________ because of the thunderstorm.
questions.tip: 'Called off' means cancelled something that had been arranged.

questions.q: I missed two weeks of school and had to __________ on my work.
questions.tip: 'Catch up' means to reach the same point as everybody else after falling behind.

questions.q: I __________ an old photograph while clearing the drawer.
questions.tip: 'Came across' means found something by chance, without looking for it.

questions.q: The doctor advised him to __________ sugary drinks.
questions.tip: 'Cut down on' means to have less of something than before.

questions.q: Please __________ this form and return it by Friday.
questions.tip: 'Fill in' means to write the details that are asked for in the spaces on a form.

questions.q: We only __________ the truth much later.
questions.tip: 'Found out' means discovered or learnt something you did not know before.

questions.q: She __________ everyone in her new class within a week.
questions.tip: 'Got along with' means had a friendly, easy relationship with people.

questions.q: It took him months to __________ his grandfather's death.
questions.tip: 'Get over' means to recover from something painful or upsetting.

questions.q: Never __________ to a bully — tell a teacher instead.
questions.tip: 'Give in' means to stop resisting and do what somebody is forcing you to do.

questions.q: Don't __________ — you are nearly at the top of the hill.
questions.tip: 'Give up' means to stop trying before you have finished.

questions.q: She __________ a difficult year but never complained.
questions.tip: 'Went through' means lived through a hard or painful experience.

questions.q: Please __________ your homework before the bell rings.
questions.tip: 'Hand in' means to give your work to the teacher or person in charge.

questions.q: I cannot __________ him; he cycles far too fast.
questions.tip: 'Keep up with' means to go as fast as someone else and stay level with them.

questions.q: I am __________ the school holidays.
questions.tip: 'Looking forward to' means feeling pleased and excited about something that is going to happen.

questions.q: The police are __________ the missing bicycle.
questions.tip: 'Looking into' means investigating something carefully to find out the truth.

questions.q: __________ the word in a dictionary if you are unsure.
questions.tip: 'Look up' means to search for information in a dictionary, book or list.

questions.q: He __________ an excuse rather than admit he had forgotten.
questions.tip: 'Made up' means invented something that is not true.

questions.q: He finally __________ to breaking the vase.
questions.tip: 'Owned up' means admitted honestly that you did something wrong.

questions.q: Her grandfather __________ peacefully last winter.
questions.tip: 'Passed away' is a gentler, kinder way of saying that someone died.

questions.q: My father will __________ me __________ after training.
questions.tip: 'Pick up' means to collect someone, usually in a car, and take them home.

questions.q: The trip was __________ until the weather improves.
questions.tip: 'Put off' means delayed something until a later time.

questions.q: I cannot __________ the constant drilling next door.
questions.tip: 'Put up with' means to bear something annoying without complaining.

questions.q: We __________ milk halfway through the recipe.
questions.tip: 'Ran out of' means used up all of something, so none was left.

questions.q: We __________ at five in the morning to avoid the traffic.
questions.tip: 'Set off' means started a journey.

questions.q: Mei __________ her mother — they have the same laugh.
questions.tip: 'Takes after' means looks or behaves like an older relative, such as a parent.

questions.q: Over a hundred pupils __________ the competition.
questions.tip: 'Took part in' means joined in and was one of the people doing it.

questions.q: He __________ the offer because the hours did not suit him.
questions.tip: 'Turned down' means refused or rejected an offer.

questions.q: Only six people __________ for the meeting.
questions.tip: 'Turned up' means arrived or appeared, often when numbers were uncertain.

questions.q: The teacher asked us to __________ our textbooks to page forty.
questions.tip: 'Turn to' means to open a book at a particular page.

questions.q: The alarm __________ at six every morning.
questions.tip: 'Goes off' means suddenly makes a loud noise, which is what alarms and bells do.

questions.q: Please __________ your shoes before entering.
questions.tip: 'Take off' means to remove something you are wearing, such as shoes or a jacket.

questions.q: She __________ painting after she retired.
questions.tip: 'Took up' means started a new hobby or activity.

questions.q: The rumour __________ quickly around the school.
questions.tip: 'Got round' means spread from person to person until everybody knew.

questions.q: He __________ his mistake and apologised at once.
questions.tip: 'Owned up to' means admitted that you were responsible for something wrong.

questions.q: The meeting was __________ to next Tuesday.
questions.tip: 'Put back' means moved an arrangement to a later time than planned.

questions.q: I need to __________ these old clothes.
questions.tip: 'Throw away' means to get rid of something you no longer want.

questions.q: Please __________ the lights when you leave the room.
questions.tip: 'Switch off' means to turn something electrical off so it stops working.

questions.q: We must __________ the problem before it gets worse.
questions.tip: 'Deal with' means to take action to sort out a problem.

questions.q: My teacher gave me some useful __________ (advice / advise).
questions.tip: The noun ends in -ce.

questions.q: I would __________ (advice / advise) you to check your work.
questions.tip: The verb ends in -se.

questions.q: The rain did not __________ (affect / effect) our plans.
questions.tip: Affect = Action (verb).

questions.q: The new rule had little __________ (affect / effect).
questions.tip: The noun is 'effect'.

questions.q: Everyone came __________ (accept / except) Nadia.
questions.tip: Except = excluding.

questions.q: Please __________ (accept / except) my apology.
The car's __________ (brake / break) failed on the slope.
questions.tip: A brake stops a car.

questions.q: Be careful not to __________ (brake / break) the glass.
Take a deep __________ (breath / breathe) and relax.
questions.tip: The noun has no final e.

questions.q: It is hard to __________ (breath / breathe) in this haze.
questions.tip: The verb ends in -the.

questions.q: They travelled across the __________ (desert / dessert) by camel.
questions.tip: One s for the dry land.

questions.q: We had ice cream for __________ (desert / dessert).
questions.tip: Two s for sweet stuff.

questions.q: The dog buried __________ (its / it's) bone.
__________ (Its / It's) almost time to go.
Please __________ (lie / lay) the book on the table.
questions.tip: You lay something down.

questions.q: I need to __________ (lie / lay) down for a while.
questions.tip: You lie down yourself.

questions.q: My shoelace is __________ (loose / lose).
questions.tip: Two o's, not tight.

questions.q: Be careful not to __________ (loose / lose) your ticket.
We walked __________ (passed / past) the old library.
questions.tip: 'Past' shows position.

questions.q: He __________ (passed / past) the examination easily.
questions.tip: The verb is 'passed'.

questions.q: May I have a __________ (peace / piece) of cake?
questions.tip: A pie-ce of pie.

questions.q: The library is a place of __________ (peace / piece) and quiet.
I must __________ (practice / practise) the piano tonight.
questions.tip: The verb ends in -se.

questions.q: Choir __________ (practice / practise) is on Wednesdays.
questions.tip: The noun ends in -ce.

questions.q: Our __________ (principal / principle) spoke at assembly.
questions.tip: The principal is your pal.

questions.q: Honesty is an important __________ (principal / principle).
questions.tip: A principle is a rule.

questions.q: Please be __________ (quiet / quite) in the library.
The test was __________ (quiet / quite) difficult.
The bus remained __________ (stationary / stationery) for ten minutes.
questions.tip: -ary means not moving.

questions.q: I bought pens and paper at the __________ (stationary / stationery) shop.
questions.tip: -ery for envelopes.

questions.q: __________ (Their / There / They're) bags are in the hall.
questions.tip: Shows belonging.

questions.q: __________ (Their / There / They're) coming at six.
questions.tip: = they are.

questions.q: Put the box over __________ (their / there / they're).
questions.tip: Shows place.

questions.q: The __________ (weather / whether) was perfect for a picnic.
I do not know __________ (weather / whether) to go.
questions.tip: = if.

questions.q: __________ (Whose / Who's) bag is this?
questions.tip: Shows belonging, no apostrophe.

questions.q: __________ (Whose / Who's) coming to the party?
questions.tip: = who is.

questions.q: __________ (Your / You're) going to enjoy this.
questions.tip: = you are.

questions.q: Is this __________ (your / you're) pencil case?
She felt a pang of __________ (conscience / conscious) after lying.
questions.tip: Your conscience knows right from wrong.

questions.q: Please __________ an effort to arrive on time.
questions.tip: Make an effort.

questions.q: He __________ a mistake in the last question.
She has __________ excellent progress this term.
questions.tip: Make progress, not do progress.

questions.q: I have to __________ my homework before dinner.
questions.tip: Do homework.

questions.q: Could you __________ me a favour?
questions.tip: Do a favour.

questions.q: Let's __________ a break for ten minutes.
questions.tip: Take a break.

questions.q: He refused to __________ a risk.
Please __________ notes during the talk.
You should __________ my advice.
questions.tip: Take advice, give advice.

questions.q: We __________ an argument about the rules.
questions.tip: Have an argument.

questions.q: Please __________ attention to the instructions.
questions.tip: Pay attention.

questions.q: We will __________ a visit to Grandmother on Sunday.
questions.tip: Pay a visit.

questions.q: He always __________ his promises.
questions.tip: Keep a promise.

questions.q: Can you __________ a secret?
Please __________ calm and wait your turn.
I hope we can __________ in touch after you move.
You will __________ a cold if you stay in wet clothes.
questions.tip: Catch a cold.

questions.q: We ran fast to __________ the bus.
The athlete __________ the world record last year.
questions.tip: Break a record.

questions.q: He __________ his promise and did not turn up.
There was __________ rain throughout the night.
questions.tip: Heavy rain, not big rain.

questions.q: We were stuck in __________ traffic for an hour.
A __________ wind blew the umbrella inside out.
questions.tip: Strong wind.

questions.q: She has a __________ opinion about recycling.
After the long walk he fell into a __________ sleep.
questions.tip: Deep sleep.

questions.q: Take a __________ breath before you begin.
I am __________ grateful for all your help.
questions.tip: Deeply grateful.

questions.q: The restaurant is __________ recommended.
questions.tip: Highly recommended.

questions.q: She was __________ disappointed by the result.
questions.tip: Bitterly disappointed.

questions.q: The speaker __________ a speech at the ceremony.
questions.tip: Give a speech.
